sources.name: MIDH Operational Guidelines 2025, Annexure V: cost norms and pattern of assistance, protected cultivation
sources.publisher: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India (Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture)
sources.note: The cost of each growing method a square metre or a hectare, the share the scheme assists (50%) and the largest area assisted for one farmer. Guidelines dated 31.12.2024, pp. 54-57. The cost norm is the ceiling the subsidy is worked on, not a quotation.

assumed: What a method does to heat, cold, light and water is a starter value set here from general practice, not a measurement: an agronomist has not reviewed it. The costs are the scheme's norms.

methods.name: Plastic mulch with drip
methods.what: A plastic sheet over the bed with drip lines under it: less water lost, fewer weeds.

ref.where: Annexure V, protected cultivation, item 10 (mulching), p. 57. Drip itself is assisted separately, under Per Drop More Crop.

methods.name: Raised beds and drains
methods.what: Beds raised above the field with drains between them, so water does not stand at the roots.

methods.name: Plastic low tunnel
methods.what: A low plastic cover over the rows in the cold months: warmer nights and no frost on the crop.

ref.where: Annexure V, protected cultivation, item 3 (plastic tunnels), p. 56

methods.name: Shade net house
methods.what: A frame covered with a net that cuts about half the sun: cooler days and less water lost.

ref.where: Annexure V, protected cultivation, item 2(a) (shade net house, tubular structure), p. 55

methods.name: Naturally ventilated polyhouse
methods.what: A plastic-covered house with open vents: no rain on the crop and warmer nights, but hotter days in summer.

ref.where: Annexure V, protected cultivation, item 1(b)(i) (naturally ventilated, tubular structure, above 1,008 m²), p. 55

methods.name: Hydroponics in a polyhouse
methods.what: Plants in channels of nutrient water inside a polyhouse: the soil no longer matters, the skill and the power supply do.

ref.where: Annexure V, protected cultivation, item 1(b)(i) with add-on 11(i) (hydroponics, Rs 350 a m² on the polyhouse), pp. 55, 57

routes.name: Government purchase at the minimum support price
routes.how: When the market falls below the support price, the state opens purchase centres (in Andhra Pradesh through the Rythu Seva Kendram). Register the crop in e-Crop first: purchase is only from registered farmers.

routes.name: The regulated market yard (mandi)
routes.how: Open auction at the nearest agricultural market yard. Dry and grade the produce first: the price is set on the lot's quality that day.

routes.name: e-NAM, the online market
routes.how: Yards linked to e-NAM put the lot before traders from other markets too. Ask at the yard whether your crop is traded on it there.

routes.name: Rythu Bazaar: straight to the people who eat it
routes.how: Farmers' markets in the towns of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana where growers sell vegetables and fruit themselves, with no commission. It needs a grower card from the estate officer, and someone to stand at the stall.

routes.name: A farmer producer organisation
routes.how: A group of farmers that pools the crop and sells in bulk, to a processor or a far market. It matters most for a new crop: one farmer's small lot finds no buyer, a group's does.

routes.name: A processor or a buyer under contract
routes.how: A mill, a pulp or pickle unit, a seed company or an exporter's packhouse that agrees the price and quality before sowing. For a crop the local yard does not trade, find this buyer before you plant.
